plain_rules:
BUY (paper) only when, on a closed 5-min candle: price is up over the last hour and above its 20-EMA; it closes above the previous hour's high; volume is at least 1.5x the hour's average; and it is no more than 5% above that breakout level (no chasing). Your rules 1-5 are checked first and always win.
STOP: the tighter of -6% and entry minus 2xATR.
TAKE PROFIT: sell 1/3 at +2R and 1/3 at +4R (R = entry minus stop); after the first trim the stop moves to break-even and the rest trails 3xATR under the high.
SELL: when the trend flips (below the 20-EMA and down over the hour), or after 3 hours with under +5%.
SIZE: risk 1% of the stack, never below the $47.50 ticket, capped by quarter-Kelly and 2% of pool liquidity.

sources.cite: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), "Time series momentum", Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250
sources.finding: An asset's own past 1-12 month return predicted its future return in all 58 futures markets studied; partially reverses later.

sources.what: Trend following over the long run
sources.cite: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), "A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing", Journal of Portfolio Management 44(1), 15-29
sources.finding: Time-series momentum had positive average returns in every decade since 1880 across 67 markets.

sources.cite: Liu & Tsyvinski (2021), "Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency", Review of Financial Studies 34(6), 2689-2727
sources.finding: Strong time-series momentum in Bitcoin, Ripple and Ethereum at daily/weekly horizons (weaker for Ethereum). Large coins only, not memecoins.

sources.cite: George & Hwang (2004), "The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing", Journal of Finance 59(5), 2145-2176
sources.finding: Nearness to the 52-week high explained much of momentum profits in US stocks.

sources.cite: Lee & Swaminathan (2000), "Price Momentum and Trading Volume", Journal of Finance 55(5), 2017-2069
sources.finding: Past volume predicts how big and how lasting momentum is; high-volume winners also reverse faster, which is why we take profits in steps.

sources.what: Cut losses 7-8%, buy within 5% of the pivot, breakout volume (practitioner)
sources.cite: William J. O'Neil, "How to Make Money in Stocks" (CAN SLIM); Investor's Business Daily
sources.finding: Practitioner rules, not a peer-reviewed study. We use a tighter -6% hard stop.

sources.cite: J. Welles Wilder (1978), "New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems"
sources.finding: Defines Average True Range; used to size stops to each coin's own volatility.

sources.cite: MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba, "Good and bad properties of the Kelly criterion"
sources.finding: Full Kelly is very volatile and error-sensitive; betting a fraction of Kelly cuts drawdowns. We cap at 1/4 Kelly.

sources.cite: Odean (1998), "Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses?", Journal of Finance (1998)
sources.finding: Retail investors hold losers too long and sell winners too early; the winners they sold kept outperforming the losers they held.

sources.cite: Marino, Naviglio, Tarantelli & Lillo (2026), "Predicting the success of new crypto-tokens: the Pump.fun case", arXiv:2602.14860
sources.finding: Only 4,338 of 655,770 Pump.fun tokens (0.63%) created Sep 2025 graduated; 92% of tokens with 30+ swaps showed at least one dump.

sources.cite: Solidus Labs (2025) report, as covered by CoinDesk, 7 May 2025
sources.finding: Reported ~98.6% of Pump.fun tokens fell below $1,000 liquidity. Industry report, disputed by Pump.fun.

backtest.verdict: Weak: on 6 trades the average trade lost -9.0% after fees and slippage. The backtest shows no edge on these coins. For comparison, buying each of the same 13 coins at its first candle and holding had a median of -87.1% and 62% of them lost money (the average is meaningless here — one or two 100x coins dominate it). Past results do not guarantee future results.
caveats: Short history: GeckoTerminal only has hours to a few days of 5-min candles for new coins.
Universe A is every migration the desk logged since it started; B is GeckoTerminal's newest PumpSwap pools.
Universe C (most-traded pools) is survivor-biased — coins that died are missing — so treat it as a best case.
In C one trade (+2083%) makes most of the profit; without it the other 24 trades average about +2%, median -4%.
Losses can exceed the -6% stop: a 5-min candle can gap through it, and fees + slippage on both sides add about 5%.
Fills assume next-candle open plus slippage; thin pools can slip far more than assumed.

Only coins with at least 25 five-minute candles (about 2 hours of trading) can be tested, so in A just 13 of 133 logged coins qualified; most of the rest died or never traded long enough — the tested sample is already the healthier part.
Rules were fixed in advance from the literature and not tuned on this data.
The desk's audit/analyst filters are not applied in the backtest (no historical RugCheck data).

forward.note: Live forward test on PAPER fills only — starts empty and grows as real signals happen.

disclaimer: No strategy guarantees profit. Most memecoins go to zero. Signals are PAPER; REAL items are suggestions you execute manually in FOMO.
